title: Draft: Follow: Improve performance
description:
Use appendPlainText(), which is orders of magnitude faster than
insertPlainText() on large documents. Apparently the latter has
some O(N) algorithm in it to find the current cursor position, even
if at the end of the document. This adds paragraphs instead of text,
so remove the newlines that we add at the end of various types so
that the output data is generally the same (it does add some extra
new lines for ASCII and UTF-8, but that actually makes the output
more similar to that of tshark.)

Create a QByteArray that uses the follow record data as source raw
data, and avoid doing deep copies as much as possible.

Use .at() and .constData() in the C-Array, Hex Dump, and YAML methods
to avoid deep copying the QByteArray. Change the ASCII sanitize_buffer
to take a refefernce to the QByteArray, and use .at() when testing it
so that it only deep copies when a non-ASCII character has to be replaced.

Related to #15963, #17313

notes.body:
This still should be relevant. From what I understand, it should speed up the collection / rendering of the follow -> udp stream  dialogue. The issue https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/19575 is still open. 

I just checked in Wireshark Version 4.2.2 (Git v4.2.2 packaged as 4.2.2-1.1build3). I opened a .pcap and tried to follow a udp stream. It still takes a very long time until I can hit the "save as" button.
This looks stale. Feel free to rebase and reopen if still valid.
